source.title_on_document: Think First, ChatGPT Later: Guiding Human–AI Collaboration for Learning Gains in Independent Human Creativity

supplement.where: No supplementary material is cited. Materials are in Appendices A to E of this PDF (pp. 33-41). Data and analysis code are on OSF: https://osf.io/t7an8/overview?view_only=fc490583cdc8458e8b895b29e4df2345 (p. 41, Data Availability).
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the main text is cited as a supplement. The OSF project holds the raw data and analysis code; all arm means, SDs, and Cohen's d for the creativity outcomes are printed in the main text (pp. 20-22).

paper_design_summary: In a lab experiment in Singapore, 196 university students (197 recruited, one excluded) were randomly assigned to solve a 12-minute product improvement task (improve a stuffed bunny) alone (human-only), with free use of ChatGPT-4 (general-AI), or with a guided 'think first, ChatGPT later' protocol (regulated-AI: 3 min own ideas, 6 min ChatGPT collaboration with sample prompts, 3 min independent refinement). All participants then solved a 12-minute product invention task (a language-learning game) without ChatGPT. Two blind expert raters scored each solution for originality, usefulness, and elaboration on 1-7 scales (Consensual Assessment Technique).

studies.label: Single lab experiment: product improvement task (with or without ChatGPT), then product invention task (all without ChatGPT)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Learning group for the product improvement task: human-only (no ChatGPT), general-AI (free ChatGPT use), or regulated-AI (guided 'think first, ChatGPT later' use)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three learning groups: human-only (control condition; n = 64), general-AI (n = 67), or regulated-AI (n = 65).

arms.name: human-only
arms.description: Solved the product improvement task independently with no other tabs or windows open (control condition); solved the later product invention task independently.

arms.name: general-AI
arms.description: Freely used ChatGPT-4 in a split-screen window for the whole 12-minute product improvement task, in any way they liked; solved the later product invention task without ChatGPT.

arms.name: regulated-AI
arms.description: 'Think first, ChatGPT later': Phase 1 (3 min) generated own initial ideas alone; Phase 2 (6 min) interacted with ChatGPT-4 as a brainstorming and feedback partner, with seven sample prompts shown; Phase 3 (3 min) independently refined and submitted one best idea. Solved the later product invention task without ChatGPT or the sample prompts.

participants.exclusions: 197 students participated; one participant who failed to adhere to the experimental instructions was excluded, leaving 196. The paper does not say in which arm the excluded participant was. The arm counts printed with the random-assignment sentence (64, 67, 65) sum to the 196 analyzed, so the paper gives no separate count at assignment.
participants.who: University students aged 18 to 29 (M = 21.62, SD = 2.09; 125 female, 67 male, 5 undisclosed) from diverse majors at a large public university, paid in course credit or money
participants.quote: Outcomes reported below are based on data from 196 participants; one participant who failed to adhere to the experimental instructions was excluded from analyses.
participants.locator: p. 8, Method, Participants; arm ns p. 8 Design and p. 20 Table 4

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, GPT-4 version, via the web interface (ChatGPT Plus subscription); default parameters, memory/model training switched off
ai_tool.how_used: General-AI: free chat use for the full 12-minute task, told to give clear, detailed prompts. Regulated-AI: chat use only in a 6-minute middle phase, after 3 minutes of independent idea generation, with instructions to treat ChatGPT as a brainstorming and feedback partner and seven illustrative sample prompts for refining, elaborating, combining, critiquing, and evaluating own ideas; final idea written independently (pp. 9-10 Table 1, p. 14, p. 42 Reproducibility Note). No AI on the second task.

task.description: Intervention: product improvement task, propose one best creative (original and useful) idea to improve an ordinary 30 cm stuffed bunny to make it more fun and raise Mattel's sales (Appendix A). Post-intervention: product invention task, invent one new game that helps adults and university students learn basic foreign-language vocabulary, with a full game design (Appendix B). A 2-minute Alternate Uses Task (car tire) was a pre-treatment baseline.
task.duration: 12 min per creative task; AUT 2 min; whole experiment about 30 min, single session (p. 13)

outcomes.measure_detail: Two trained experts, blind to condition, rated each solution 1-7 for originality relative to the pool (CAT); responses viewed in randomized order; mean of the two raters used; consistency ICC = .958. eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned to no ChatGPT, free ChatGPT, or guided ChatGPT on a creative product improvement task (p. 8). 196 people analyzed (64, 67, 65), well above 50 (p. 8). Originality, usefulness, and elaboration of each person's solution were rated by two blind experts on the AI-assisted task (with_ai) and on a later unassisted task (after_ai) (pp. 15-16, 20-22).

one_line_finding: With ChatGPT available, free use raised expert-rated originality over no AI (4.08 vs 3.06, d = 0.79) while guided use did not (3.30, d = 0.18); on a later task without ChatGPT, the guided group beat both no-AI and free-use groups in originality (3.42 vs 2.63 and 2.69, d = 0.52 and 0.48) and usefulness (d = 0.50 and 0.48), and free use did not differ from no AI (pp. 20-22).
open_questions: The arm counts at assignment are not given separately: 197 participated and 196 were analyzed, and the arm ns printed with the random-assignment sentence (64, 67, 65) sum to 196. Which arm the excluded participant came from is not stated.

For the regulated-AI arm, AI was available only during the 6-minute middle phase; the final solution was written independently in Phase 3. The with_ai outcomes for this arm therefore reflect partial AI availability (coded 'mixed' at the outcome level because the human-only arm also had no AI).

Sign convention of printed d for the general-AI vs regulated-AI comparisons on the first task (d = -0.62, -0.60, -1.13) appears to be regulated minus general; the paper does not state the formula for d.
No preregistration is mentioned; the paper calls the creativity, elaboration, and prompt analyses 'main confirmatory analyses' (p. 18).
notes: Pairwise p-values are Bonferroni-corrected; no SEs or test statistics are printed for pairwise contrasts, only means, SDs, d, and p. Arm ns come from p. 8 and Table 4 (p. 20). Fig. 2 (p. 21) plots means with standard-error bars. Baseline AUT fluency and flexibility (pre-treatment balance check, Table 3 p. 19) are not outcomes and are omitted. Self-assessed originality and usefulness, subjective experience, creative self-efficacy, and metacognition are self-reports (exploratory) and are omitted as outcomes. Prompt-type coding of ChatGPT transcripts (Table 5, p. 23) is process data, not a creativity outcome. No diversity-across-people outcome is reported. candidates.json lists a 2025 NUS bachelor's thesis by Qiu ('Think First, ChatGPT Later: Collaborative AI Use Sustains Creativity in Problem-Solving Even After Tool Removal') as another version; this PDF does not mention it, so sample_overlap is left empty.
